concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.title: SI Base Quantities & Supplementary Units
concepts.plain_formula: dθ = ds / r (rad), dΩ = dA / r² (sr)
concepts.ncert_core_rule: 7 fundamental SI base quantities define all physical measurement. Radian and steradian are supplementary dimensionless units.
concepts.author_book_nuance: H.C. Verma: A quantity can possess units without dimensions (rad, sr), but no quantity can possess dimensions without units.
concepts.neet_trap_point: Students assume all quantities with units have dimensions. Plane angle has unit radian but dimension [M^0 L^0 T^0].

trap_quiz.title: NEET Trap: Dimensionality of Radian and Steradian
trap_quiz.warning: Having units does NOT imply having physical dimensions! Radian and Steradian have recognized SI units, but are strictly dimensionless [M⁰ L⁰ T⁰].
trap_quiz.question: Which of the following statements is strictly correct regarding plane angle and solid angle in the SI system?

options.text: A) Both have units (rad, sr) but are strictly dimensionless with dimensions [M⁰ L⁰ T⁰].
options.trap: Correct: Supplementary units are pure geometric ratios (arc/r and area/r²).

options.text: B) Both have physical dimensions [L] and [L²] because they derive from arc length and surface area.
options.trap: Trap: Length and area cancel out in radius and radius-squared ratios.

options.text: C) Radian has dimension [L], while Steradian is dimensionless.
options.trap: Trap: Neither has length dimension.

options.text: D) Neither possesses units nor dimensions in modern SI convention.
options.trap: Trap: Radian and steradian are explicitly defined SI supplementary units.

trap_quiz.explanation: NCERT Section 2.2: Plane angle (dθ = ds/r) and solid angle (dΩ = dA/r²) possess units radian and steradian, yet both are strictly dimensionless with [M⁰ L⁰ T⁰].

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.title: Derived Units & Standard Metric Prefixes
concepts.ncert_core_rule: Derived units are algebraic combinations of base units. SI prefixes represent powers of 10 from 10^-15 to 10^12.
concepts.author_book_nuance: D.C. Pandey: Double prefixes are strictly forbidden in SI rules (e.g., write pF, never μμF).
concepts.neet_trap_point: Attaching prefixes to kilogram instead of gram. Since kg already has 'kilo', write 1 mg for 10^-6 kg, not 1 μkg.

trap_quiz.title: NEET Trap: Double Prefixes & Mass Prefix Attachment
trap_quiz.warning: SI conventions strictly forbid double prefixes (μμF → pF); all mass prefixes must attach to the gram, not kilogram (10⁻⁶ kg = 1 mg, never 1 μkg).
trap_quiz.question: A capacitor has capacitance 10⁻¹² F and a dust particle has mass 10⁻⁶ kg. According to standard SI conventions, how should these quantities be reported?

options.text: A) 1 pF and 1 mg, because double prefixes are forbidden and mass prefixes attach to the gram.
options.trap: Correct: Compound prefixes are illegal; mass prefixes attach to gram.

options.text: B) 1 μμF and 1 μkg, matching direct decimal multipliers.
options.trap: Trap: μμ is a double prefix (forbidden); prefix cannot attach to kilogram.

options.text: C) 1 pF and 1 μkg, since kilogram is the base standard.
options.trap: Trap: Kilogram already contains 'kilo', so prefixes attach to gram.
Trap: Violates single standard prefix convention.

trap_quiz.explanation: SI rules strictly forbid compound prefixes like μμF (must use pF). Also, because kilogram contains 'kilo', prefixes attach to the gram: 10⁻⁶ kg = 1 mg.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.title: Dimensions of Physical Quantities & Common Equivalences
concepts.ncert_core_rule: Dimensions of a physical quantity are powers to which base units are raised to represent that quantity.
concepts.author_book_nuance: Halliday & Resnick: Torque and Work share identical dimensions [M L^2 T^-2] but are fundamentally different: Torque is a vector, Work is a scalar.
concepts.neet_trap_point: Confusing quantities that share identical dimensions with being physically identical. Never equate their physical nature.

trap_quiz.title: NEET Trap: Dimensional Equivalence vs Physical Nature
trap_quiz.warning: Identical dimensions ([M L² T⁻²]) do NOT mean identical physical nature! Work is a scalar (Joules), while Torque is a rotational vector (N·m). Never add them!
trap_quiz.question: Work and Torque have identical dimensional formulas [M L² T⁻²]. Which of the following operations is physically meaningful and valid?

options.text: A) Neither adding Work to Torque nor expressing Torque in Joules is physically permissible.
options.trap: Correct: Work is scalar dot-product in Joules; Torque is vector cross-product in N·m.

options.text: B) Work and Torque can be added directly because their dimensions match.
options.trap: Trap: Having identical dimensions does not permit adding scalar energy to vector torque.

options.text: C) Torque can be expressed in Joules since 1 N·m = 1 J algebraically.
options.trap: Trap: Joule is reserved strictly for energy and scalar work.

options.text: D) Torque is a scalar quantity while Work is a vector.
options.trap: Trap: Inversion error; Torque is a vector, Work is a scalar.

trap_quiz.explanation: Work is scalar dot product (W = F · d in Joules). Torque is vector cross product (τ = r × F in N·m). They cannot be added, and Torque must never be reported in Joules.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.title: Principle of Homogeneity of Dimensions
concepts.ncert_core_rule: Physical quantities having identical dimensions alone can be added, subtracted, or equated. Arguments of trig, exp, and log functions must be dimensionless.
concepts.author_book_nuance: I.E. Irodov: In (P + a/V^2)(V - b) = RT, dimensional homogeneity dictates [a/V^2] = [P] and [b] = [V].
concepts.neet_trap_point: Assuming dimensional consistency guarantees physical correctness. Pure numbers (like 1/2 or 2π) cannot be derived or checked by dimensional analysis.

trap_quiz.title: NEET Trap: Principle of Homogeneity & Van der Waals Constants
trap_quiz.warning: In (P + a/V²)(V - b) = RT, [a/V²] = [P]. Dimensional consistency is necessary, but never sufficient to establish physical correctness.
trap_quiz.question: In the van der Waals gas equation (P + a/V²)(V - b) = RT, what are the dimensions of the constant a?

options.text: A) [M L⁵ T⁻²], derived from [a] = [P] · [V²].
options.trap: Correct: [a] = [P][V²] = [M L⁻¹ T⁻²][L³]² = [M L⁵ T⁻²].

options.text: B) [M L⁻¹ T⁻²], assuming a shares the dimensions of pressure directly.
options.trap: Trap: Forgets to multiply by V².

options.text: C) [M L⁴ T⁻²], incorrectly calculating [V²] as [L²] instead of [L³]².
options.trap: Trap: Volume V has dimension L³, so V² is L⁶.

options.text: D) [M⁰ L³ T⁰], confusing constant a with volume constant b.
options.trap: Trap: [b] = [V] = [L³], not [a].

trap_quiz.explanation: By Homogeneity, [a/V²] = [P] ==> [a] = [P][V²] = [M L⁻¹ T⁻²][L³]² = [M L⁵ T⁻²].

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.title: Classification of Errors & Mean Absolute Error
concepts.plain_formula: a_mean = (Σ a_i) / n, Δa_mean = (Σ |a_mean - a_i|) / n
concepts.ncert_core_rule: Systematic errors are unidirectional and eliminated by calibration. Random errors fluctuate and are minimized by taking the arithmetic mean of repeated readings.
concepts.author_book_nuance: H.C. Verma: Absolute error is always positive. The sum of signed deviations from the mean is always identically zero.
concepts.neet_trap_point: Taking the algebraic sum of deviations instead of the magnitude |Δa_i|, which falsely gives zero mean error.

trap_quiz.title: NEET Trap: Mean Absolute Error & The Zero Sum Trap
trap_quiz.warning: The algebraic sum of deviations Σ(a_mean - a_i) is identically zero! You MUST sum absolute magnitudes |Δa_i| to compute mean absolute error.
trap_quiz.question: In an experiment, four measurements of length are 10.2 cm, 10.4 cm, 9.8 cm, and 9.6 cm. What are the arithmetic mean and the mean absolute error?

options.text: A) Mean = 10.0 cm, Mean Absolute Error = 0.30 cm.
options.trap: Correct: Mean = 10.0 cm; deviations magnitudes are 0.2, 0.4, 0.2, 0.4; average = 1.2/4 = 0.30 cm.

options.text: B) Mean = 10.0 cm, Mean Absolute Error = 0.00 cm.
options.trap: Trap: The Zero Sum Trap! Summing signed deviations (+0.2 +0.4 -0.2 -0.4 = 0).

options.text: C) Mean = 10.0 cm, Mean Absolute Error = 0.60 cm.
options.trap: Trap: Forgets to divide the sum of magnitudes by n=4.

options.text: D) Mean = 10.1 cm, Mean Absolute Error = 0.15 cm.
options.trap: Trap: Arithmetic error in mean computation.

trap_quiz.explanation: Mean = (10.2 + 10.4 + 9.8 + 9.6)/4 = 10.0 cm. Absolute error magnitudes = |+0.2| + |+0.4| + |-0.2| + |-0.4| = 1.2 cm. Mean absolute error = 1.2/4 = 0.30 cm.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.title: Combination & Propagation of Errors (Power Rule)
concepts.latex_formula: Z = \frac{A^p B^q}{C^r} \implies \frac{\Delta Z}{Z} = p\frac{\Delta A}{A} + q\frac{\Delta B}{B} + r\frac{\Delta C}{C}
concepts.plain_formula: Z = (A^p * B^q) / C^r  ==>  ΔZ/Z = p*(ΔA/A) + q*(ΔB/B) + r*(ΔC/C)
concepts.ncert_core_rule: In worst-case error estimation, fractional errors for product, quotient, and power relations always add with their positive power coefficients.
concepts.author_book_nuance: D.C. Pandey: Even if C is in the denominator (C^r), its fractional error is added with coefficient +r, never subtracted!
concepts.neet_trap_point: Subtracting errors for quantities in the denominator. Errors always accumulate in maximum uncertainty analysis.

trap_quiz.title: NEET Trap: Error Propagation in Denominators
trap_quiz.warning: In worst-case error analysis, uncertainties NEVER cancel out! In P = A³ B² / (√C · D), the error contributions from C and D ALWAYS ADD.
trap_quiz.question: A physical quantity P = A³ B² / (√C · D). The percentage errors in A, B, C, D are 1%, 2%, 4%, 2%. What is the maximum percentage error in P?

options.text: A) 11%, because all fractional error terms reinforce each other and add.
B) 3%, because denominator errors from C and D are subtracted.
options.trap: Trap: Denominator subtraction fallacy (7% - 4% = 3%). In worst-case analysis, errors never subtract!

options.text: C) 7%, forgetting the square root factor on C.
options.trap: Trap: Missing exponent power factor.

options.text: D) 15%, squaring percentage errors.
options.trap: Trap: Confusing linear power rule with standard deviation.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.title: Measuring Instruments: Vernier Callipers & Screw Gauge
concepts.plain_formula: LC = Pitch / Circular Divisions, True = Observed - (±Zero Error)
concepts.ncert_citation: NCERT Class 11 Part 1, Chapter 2 Appendix & Practical Manual
concepts.ncert_core_rule: Vernier LC = 1 MSD - 1 VSD. Screw gauge LC = Pitch / Total circular divisions. True reading = Observed reading - (Zero Error).
concepts.author_book_nuance: NCERT Lab Manual: Positive zero error is SUBTRACTED; negative zero error is ADDED (- (-e) = +e).
concepts.neet_trap_point: Inverting zero error signs: Positive zero error (+e) must be subtracted, while negative zero error (-e) must be added.

trap_quiz.title: NEET Trap: Zero Error Sign Convention in Vernier & Screw Gauge
trap_quiz.warning: True Reading = Observed Reading - (Zero Error). Positive zero error is SUBTRACTED; negative zero error is ADDED!
trap_quiz.question: A screw gauge with least count 0.01 mm has a negative zero error of -0.04 mm. When measuring a wire, the main scale reads 3 mm and the 42nd circular division coincides with the datum line. What is the true diameter?

options.text: A) 3.46 mm, because subtracting a negative zero error adds 0.04 mm to observed reading (3.42 - (-0.04)).
options.trap: Correct: Observed = 3.42 mm; True = 3.42 - (-0.04) = 3.46 mm.

options.text: B) 3.38 mm, incorrectly subtracting the magnitude of negative zero error (3.42 - 0.04).
options.trap: Trap: Inverting negative error sign; subtracting instead of adding.

options.text: C) 3.42 mm, ignoring zero error correction entirely.
options.trap: Trap: Fails to apply zero error correction.

options.text: D) 3.82 mm, misreading circular scale division contribution.
options.trap: Trap: Scaling error.

trap_quiz.explanation: Observed reading = PSR + (CSR × LC) = 3 mm + (42 × 0.01 mm) = 3.42 mm. True reading = Observed - Zero Error = 3.42 - (-0.04) = 3.46 mm.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.title: Significant Figures & Arithmetic Rounding Rules
concepts.latex_formula: \text{Add/Sub: Least Decimal Places}, \quad \text{Mul/Div: Least Significant Figures}
concepts.plain_formula: Add/Sub: Retain least decimal places | Mul/Div: Retain least significant figures
concepts.ncert_core_rule: Significant figures reflect measurement precision. Leading zeros are never significant; trailing zeros with a decimal point are significant.
concepts.author_book_nuance: H.C. Verma: In addition 100.1 + 0.003 = 100.103 -> 100.1 (1 decimal place). Do not count total significant figures in addition/subtraction.
concepts.neet_trap_point: Applying the multiplication rule (least sig figs) to addition/subtraction, which is governed strictly by the least decimal places.

trap_quiz.title: NEET Trap: Significant Figures in Subtraction (NEET 2020)
trap_quiz.warning: In addition/subtraction (9.99 m - 0.0099 m), round to LEAST DECIMAL PLACES, not significant figures!
trap_quiz.question: Taking into account the significant figures, what is the value of 9.99 m - 0.0099 m? (NEET 2020 PYQ)

options.text: A) 9.98 m, because 9.99 has 2 decimal places, dictating 2 decimal places in the final result.
options.trap: Correct: Governed strictly by least decimal places (2 decimals).

options.text: B) 9.980 m, mistakenly keeping 4 significant figures.
options.trap: Trap: Applies multiplication rule instead of addition/subtraction rule.

options.text: C) 9.9 m, mistakenly rounding to the fewest significant figures.
options.trap: Trap: Confuses decimal place rule with sig fig rule.

options.text: D) 9.9801 m, retaining all calculated digits without rounding.
options.trap: Trap: Ignores NCERT precision limits.

trap_quiz.explanation: NCERT Rule: In addition/subtraction, the result retains as many decimal places as there are in the number with the least decimal places. 9.99 m has 2 decimal places, so 9.9801 m rounds to 9.98 m.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.title: Position-Time Graphs
concepts.ncert_core_rule: Slope of the position-time curve represents instantaneous velocity.
concepts.author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 3: Negative slope indicates velocity in opposite direction, not necessarily deceleration.
concepts.neet_trap_point: Confusing slope of x-t graph (velocity) with slope of v-t graph (acceleration).

trap_quiz.title: NEET Trap: Position-Time Graphs
trap_quiz.warning: Confusing slope of x-t graph (velocity) with slope of v-t graph (acceleration).
trap_quiz.question: In a standard NEET problem on 'Position-Time Graphs', which of the following statements represents the critical condition to prevent sign or angle errors?

options.text: A) Verify coordinate axes orientation and component reference angle before applying formula.
options.trap: Correct: Prevents sine/cosine and +/- direction inversion.

options.text: B) The textbook scalar equation applies universally in all reference frames.
options.trap: Trap: Scalar equations fail when acceleration changes or frame is non-inertial.

options.text: C) Gravitational acceleration g is always negative regardless of chosen axis.
options.trap: Trap: Sign of g depends strictly on positive axis definition.

options.text: D) Horizontal velocity component alters vertical flight duration.
options.trap: Trap: Horizontal and vertical motions are strictly independent.

trap_quiz.explanation: Key Rule: Slope of the position-time curve represents instantaneous velocity. HCV Ch 3: Negative slope indicates velocity in opposite direction, not necessarily deceleration.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.title: Resolution of Vectors
concepts.ncert_core_rule: Any 2D vector can be resolved into two mutually perpendicular orthogonal components.
concepts.author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 2: Components of a vector behave independently along x and y coordinates.
concepts.neet_trap_point: Assigning cosine to vertical axis when angle was given with horizontal.

trap_quiz.title: NEET Trap: Resolution of Vectors
trap_quiz.warning: Assigning cosine to vertical axis when angle was given with horizontal.
trap_quiz.question: In a standard NEET problem on 'Resolution of Vectors', which of the following statements represents the critical condition to prevent sign or angle errors?

options.text: A) Verify coordinate axes orientation and component reference angle before applying formula.
options.trap: Correct: Prevents sine/cosine and +/- direction inversion.

options.text: B) The textbook scalar equation applies universally in all reference frames.
options.trap: Trap: Scalar equations fail when acceleration changes or frame is non-inertial.

options.text: C) Gravitational acceleration g is always negative regardless of chosen axis.
options.trap: Trap: Sign of g depends strictly on positive axis definition.

options.text: D) Horizontal velocity component alters vertical flight duration.
options.trap: Trap: Horizontal and vertical motions are strictly independent.

trap_quiz.explanation: Key Rule: Any 2D vector can be resolved into two mutually perpendicular orthogonal components. HCV Ch 2: Components of a vector behave independently along x and y coordinates.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.title: Time of Flight
concepts.ncert_core_rule: Time of flight is determined purely by the vertical component of initial velocity.
concepts.author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 3: The horizontal velocity component vx has zero acceleration and does not affect the time spent in the air.
concepts.neet_trap_point: Question specifies angle with vertical axis instead of horizontal (swapping sin with cos).

trap_quiz.title: Horizontal Acceleration Assumption Trap
trap_quiz.warning: Students frequently try to incorporate horizontal speed vx into time of flight calculations.
trap_quiz.question: Two projectiles are launched from the same point with different launch angles and initial speeds, but both attain the exact same maximum height H. What is the ratio of their times of flight T₁ / T₂?

options.trap: Correct: Both reach same H_max => same initial vertical velocity vy0 => same time of flight T = 2vy0/g.
Trap: Assumed time depends on range or horizontal speed.

options.text: C) Dependent on launch angle θ
options.trap: Trap: Failed to realize H_max determines vy0 independently of θ.
Incorrect ratio inversion.

trap_quiz.explanation: Since H_max = vy²/(2g), same H_max strictly means same vertical speed vy. Time of flight T = 2vy/g depends exclusively on vertical speed. Therefore T1/T2 = 1:1, regardless of their ranges or horizontal components!

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.title: The Max Height Arc
concepts.ncert_core_rule: At maximum height, the vertical component of velocity is zero while horizontal velocity remains v0*cos(theta).
concepts.author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 3: Speed at the top is not zero; it equals v0*cos(theta). Kinetic energy is minimum but non-zero.
concepts.neet_trap_point: Confusing total velocity being zero with only vertical velocity component being zero at top of trajectory.

trap_quiz.title: Swapping Sine and Cosine (Angle with Vertical Axis)
trap_quiz.warning: The textbook formula H_max = (v0² sin²θ)/(2g) is valid ONLY when θ is measured from the horizontal! If measured from vertical, vertical speed is v0 cos θ, turning sin²θ into cos²θ.
trap_quiz.question: A projectile is launched with velocity v₀ = 50 m/s at an angle of 30° with the VERTICAL. What is the maximum vertical height reached? (Take g = 10 m/s²)

options.trap: Trap: Applied sin²(30°) blindly instead of vertical component!
Correct: Uses cos²(30°) = 0.75 for vertical motion.
Incorrect: Assumed pure vertical projection.
Incorrect: Arithmetic error in squaring velocity.

trap_quiz.explanation: Since angle is given with the vertical axis, the vertical velocity component is vy = v0·cos(30°) = 50·(√3/2) = 25√3 m/s. H_max = vy²/(2g) = (25√3)² / 20 = (625·3)/20 = 1875/20 = 93.75 m. Option A (31.25 m) is the exact trap distractor chosen by students who didn't read 'with vertical'!

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.title: Horizontal Range and Complementary Angles
concepts.ncert_core_rule: Horizontal range is identical for complementary projection angles theta and (90 - theta) at the same initial speed.
concepts.author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 3: Although ranges are equal for theta and 90-theta, maximum heights and times of flight are strictly unequal.
concepts.neet_trap_point: Assuming time of flight and maximum height are also equal when ranges are equal for complementary angles.

trap_quiz.title: NEET Trap: Horizontal Range and Complementary Angles
trap_quiz.warning: Assuming time of flight and maximum height are also equal when ranges are equal for complementary angles.
trap_quiz.question: In a standard NEET problem on 'Horizontal Range and Complementary Angles', which of the following statements represents the critical condition to prevent sign or angle errors?

options.text: A) Verify coordinate axes orientation and component reference angle before applying formula.
options.trap: Correct: Prevents sine/cosine and +/- direction inversion.

options.text: B) The textbook scalar equation applies universally in all reference frames.
options.trap: Trap: Scalar equations fail when acceleration changes or frame is non-inertial.

options.text: C) Gravitational acceleration g is always negative regardless of chosen axis.
options.trap: Trap: Sign of g depends strictly on positive axis definition.

options.text: D) Horizontal velocity component alters vertical flight duration.
options.trap: Trap: Horizontal and vertical motions are strictly independent.

trap_quiz.explanation: Key Rule: Horizontal range is identical for complementary projection angles theta and (90 - theta) at the same initial speed. HCV Ch 3: Although ranges are equal for theta and 90-theta, maximum heights and times of flight are strictly unequal.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.title: Equation of Trajectory
concepts.plain_formula: y = x · tan(θ) - (g · x²) / (2 · v₀² · cos²(θ))
concepts.ncert_core_rule: The trajectory of a projectile is parabolic in nature, relating vertical coordinate y to horizontal coordinate x.
concepts.author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 3: Alternative formulation y = x*tan(theta)*(1 - x/R) simplifies range-based NEET problems instantly.
concepts.neet_trap_point: Confusing tan(theta) factor with cot(theta) when comparing experimental trajectory equations.

trap_quiz.title: NEET Trap: Equation of Trajectory
trap_quiz.warning: Confusing tan(theta) factor with cot(theta) when comparing experimental trajectory equations.
trap_quiz.question: In a standard NEET problem on 'Equation of Trajectory', which of the following statements represents the critical condition to prevent sign or angle errors?

options.text: A) Verify coordinate axes orientation and component reference angle before applying formula.
options.trap: Correct: Prevents sine/cosine and +/- direction inversion.

options.text: B) The textbook scalar equation applies universally in all reference frames.
options.trap: Trap: Scalar equations fail when acceleration changes or frame is non-inertial.

options.text: C) Gravitational acceleration g is always negative regardless of chosen axis.
options.trap: Trap: Sign of g depends strictly on positive axis definition.

options.text: D) Horizontal velocity component alters vertical flight duration.
options.trap: Trap: Horizontal and vertical motions are strictly independent.

trap_quiz.explanation: Key Rule: The trajectory of a projectile is parabolic in nature, relating vertical coordinate y to horizontal coordinate x. HCV Ch 3: Alternative formulation y = x*tan(theta)*(1 - x/R) simplifies range-based NEET problems instantly.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.title: Centripetal Acceleration
concepts.ncert_core_rule: Acceleration in uniform circular motion always points radially inward toward the center of the circle.
concepts.author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 7: Speed is constant but velocity continuously changes direction; therefore acceleration is non-zero and perpendicular to velocity.
concepts.neet_trap_point: Assuming acceleration is zero because speed is constant in uniform circular motion.

trap_quiz.title: NEET Trap: Centripetal Acceleration
trap_quiz.warning: Assuming acceleration is zero because speed is constant in uniform circular motion.
trap_quiz.question: In a standard NEET problem on 'Centripetal Acceleration', which of the following statements represents the critical condition to prevent sign or angle errors?

options.text: A) Verify coordinate axes orientation and component reference angle before applying formula.
options.trap: Correct: Prevents sine/cosine and +/- direction inversion.

options.text: B) The textbook scalar equation applies universally in all reference frames.
options.trap: Trap: Scalar equations fail when acceleration changes or frame is non-inertial.

options.text: C) Gravitational acceleration g is always negative regardless of chosen axis.
options.trap: Trap: Sign of g depends strictly on positive axis definition.

options.text: D) Horizontal velocity component alters vertical flight duration.
options.trap: Trap: Horizontal and vertical motions are strictly independent.

trap_quiz.explanation: Key Rule: Acceleration in uniform circular motion always points radially inward toward the center of the circle. HCV Ch 7: Speed is constant but velocity continuously changes direction; therefore acceleration is non-zero and perpendicular to velocity.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.title: Velocity-Time Graphs & Displacement
concepts.ncert_core_rule: Area under velocity-time graph equals displacement; slope equals acceleration.
concepts.author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 3: Negative area represents negative displacement, not distance traveled.
concepts.neet_trap_point: Calculating distance instead of displacement by ignoring sign of negative area!

trap_quiz.title: NEET Trap: Velocity-Time Graphs & Displacement
trap_quiz.warning: Calculating distance instead of displacement by ignoring sign of negative area!
trap_quiz.question: In a standard NEET problem on 'Velocity-Time Graphs & Displacement', which of the following statements represents the critical condition to prevent sign or angle errors?

options.text: A) Verify coordinate axes orientation and component reference angle before applying formula.
options.trap: Correct: Prevents sine/cosine and +/- direction inversion.

options.text: C) Gravitational acceleration g is always negative regardless of chosen axis.
options.trap: Trap: Sign of g depends strictly on positive axis definition.

options.text: D) Horizontal velocity component alters vertical flight duration.
options.trap: Trap: Horizontal and vertical motions are strictly independent.

trap_quiz.explanation: Key Rule: Area under velocity-time graph equals displacement; slope equals acceleration. HCV Ch 3: Negative area represents negative displacement, not distance traveled.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.title: Relative Velocity & River-Boat Vectors
concepts.ncert_core_rule: Relative velocity of object A with respect to B is vector difference v_A - v_B.
concepts.author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 3: Shortest time to cross river requires heading directly perpendicular to flow.
concepts.neet_trap_point: Confusing shortest path with shortest time in river-boat problems!

trap_quiz.title: NEET Trap: Relative Velocity & River-Boat Vectors
trap_quiz.warning: Confusing shortest path with shortest time in river-boat problems!
trap_quiz.question: In a standard NEET problem on 'Relative Velocity & River-Boat Vectors', which of the following statements represents the critical condition to prevent sign or angle errors?

options.trap: Trap: Scalar equations fail when acceleration changes or frame is non-inertial.

options.text: C) Gravitational acceleration g is always negative regardless of chosen axis.
options.trap: Trap: Sign of g depends strictly on positive axis definition.

options.text: D) Horizontal velocity component alters vertical flight duration.
options.trap: Trap: Horizontal and vertical motions are strictly independent.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.title: Horizontal Projection from a Height
concepts.plain_formula: t = sqrt(2h / g), R = v₀ · sqrt(2h / g)
concepts.ncert_core_rule: Vertical motion is identical to free fall from height h; initial vertical velocity is zero.
concepts.author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 3: Horizontal speed v0 has zero effect on the time taken to hit the ground.
concepts.neet_trap_point: Believing a faster launched projectile takes longer to hit the ground than one dropped!

trap_quiz.title: NEET Trap: Horizontal Projection from a Height
trap_quiz.warning: Believing a faster launched projectile takes longer to hit the ground than one dropped!
trap_quiz.question: In a standard NEET problem on 'Horizontal Projection from a Height', which of the following statements represents the critical condition to prevent sign or angle errors?

options.text: A) Verify coordinate axes orientation and component reference angle before applying formula.
options.trap: Correct: Prevents sine/cosine and +/- direction inversion.

options.text: B) The textbook scalar equation applies universally in all reference frames.
options.trap: Trap: Scalar equations fail when acceleration changes or frame is non-inertial.

options.text: C) Gravitational acceleration g is always negative regardless of chosen axis.
options.trap: Trap: Sign of g depends strictly on positive axis definition.

options.text: D) Horizontal velocity component alters vertical flight duration.
options.trap: Trap: Horizontal and vertical motions are strictly independent.

trap_quiz.explanation: Key Rule: Vertical motion is identical to free fall from height h; initial vertical velocity is zero. HCV Ch 3: Horizontal speed v0 has zero effect on the time taken to hit the ground.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.title: Projectile on an Inclined Plane
concepts.ncert_core_rule: Resolve g into components parallel (g sin beta) and perpendicular (g cos beta) to incline.
concepts.author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 3: Treat incline as new x-axis with effective gravity components.
concepts.neet_trap_point: Forgetting that acceleration along incline is non-zero (g sin beta)!

trap_quiz.title: NEET Trap: Projectile on an Inclined Plane
trap_quiz.warning: Forgetting that acceleration along incline is non-zero (g sin beta)!
trap_quiz.question: In a standard NEET problem on 'Projectile on an Inclined Plane', which of the following statements represents the critical condition to prevent sign or angle errors?

options.text: A) Verify coordinate axes orientation and component reference angle before applying formula.
options.trap: Correct: Prevents sine/cosine and +/- direction inversion.

options.text: B) The textbook scalar equation applies universally in all reference frames.
options.trap: Trap: Scalar equations fail when acceleration changes or frame is non-inertial.

options.text: C) Gravitational acceleration g is always negative regardless of chosen axis.
options.trap: Trap: Sign of g depends strictly on positive axis definition.

options.text: D) Horizontal velocity component alters vertical flight duration.
options.trap: Trap: Horizontal and vertical motions are strictly independent.

trap_quiz.explanation: Key Rule: Resolve g into components parallel (g sin beta) and perpendicular (g cos beta) to incline. HCV Ch 3: Treat incline as new x-axis with effective gravity components.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.title: Radius of Curvature at Apex
concepts.ncert_core_rule: Radius of curvature equals speed squared divided by normal acceleration component.
concepts.author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 3: At apex, total speed is vx = v0 cos theta and gravity g is purely normal.
concepts.neet_trap_point: Using total launch speed v0 instead of horizontal velocity v0 cos theta at the apex!

trap_quiz.warning: Using total launch speed v0 instead of horizontal velocity v0 cos theta at the apex!

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.title: Angular Velocity & Linear Speed Relation
concepts.ncert_core_rule: Linear speed is directly proportional to radius r for particles on a rotating rigid body.
concepts.author_book_nuance: HCV Ch 7: All points on a rotating wheel have the same omega but different linear speeds v.
concepts.neet_trap_point: Thinking points closer to center move with higher linear velocity than the outer rim!

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.title: Non-Uniform Circular Motion Acceleration
concepts.ncert_core_rule: Total acceleration has two orthogonal components: radial (centripetal) and tangential.

concepts.neet_trap_point: Forgetting tangential acceleration when speed is increasing in circular motion!

trap_quiz.title: NEET Trap: [Dual Nature of Matter & Radiation] Concept 8
trap_quiz.warning: Common exam pitfall in applying [Dual Nature of Matter & Radiation] Concept 8.
trap_quiz.question: In a standard NEET problem on '[Dual Nature of Matter & Radiation] Concept 8', which of the following statements represents the critical condition to prevent sign or angle errors?

options.text: A) Verify coordinate axes orientation and component reference angle before applying formula.
options.trap: Correct: Prevents sine/cosine and +/- direction inversion.

options.text: B) The textbook scalar equation applies universally in all reference frames.
options.trap: Trap: Scalar equations fail when acceleration changes or frame is non-inertial.

options.text: C) Gravitational acceleration g is always negative regardless of chosen axis.
options.trap: Trap: Sign of g depends strictly on positive axis definition.

options.text: D) Horizontal velocity component alters vertical flight duration.
options.trap: Trap: Horizontal and vertical motions are strictly independent.
